It forms an island-like vignette of painted habitat: a clearly visible wide band of pale cracked dried mud around clear shallow blue-green water, a few fresh grass shoots and meadow plants, softly painted banks fading into transparency. Several similarly sized tiny froglets that just completed metamorphosis climb out onto mud, some with short tail stubs; a few tadpoles are visible in the water. On a flat stone at the edge sits the spotted frog ecologist, holding its blank cream notebook and a completely unmarked plain wooden measuring strip, observing the froglets with warm curiosity. Blue-green dragonfly assistant hovers nearby. Keep froglets similar in size; do not suggest any treatment comparison or result. The pool's dried-and-refilled margin is unmistakable. No distant panorama or sky; close self-contained habitat scene, broad simple forms readable at text width.

A small shallow pool in a Central European meadow in early summer, recently refilled after drying out: a wide band of cracked, pale dried mud surrounds the water, with fresh green shoots at the edge and a few puddles. Several tiny froglets that have just finished metamorphosis climb out of the water onto the mud, some still with short tail stubs; a few tadpoles are visible in the clear shallow water. On a flat stone at the edge, a plains leopard frog field ecologist (brown-green frog with dark rounded spots and pale ridges along the back) holds a small blank field notebook and a wooden ruler and watches the froglets with curiosity; a blue-green dragonfly assistant hovers beside it. Gentle academic humour, natural anatomy, soft daylight. The froglets are all of similar size; do not suggest that any of them is larger or smaller. No text, letters, numbers, labels, charts, logos or watermarks; course brand colours only as small accents.

Indigo #5D2890, amethyst #86579E and orange #F3A712 may appear only as tiny accents, never large areas. No axes, ticks, ruler graduations, written marks, numerical results or comparative outcome cues. Notebook pages and wooden ruler completely blank. Frog has anatomically plausible limbs; dragonfly has six legs and four clear wings. All small froglets similar in size and appearance. Quiet, legible composition at printed text width. No border or text.
